prompt.context: A large auto insurance company, AutoDrivers, is exploring telematics and has identified whether OBD (On-Board Diagnostics) or a mobile solution is the right fit for them. Telematics is defined as the convergence of informatics and telecommunications to transmit data — think Fitbit or OnStar, which collect and use data to deliver additional services to consumers. With telematics, AutoDrivers can capture driving data and use it to better price insurance premiums. The company hopes that using telematics will enable it to enroll new customers and reverse its decline in market share. AutoDrivers is a medium-size auto insurance company operating mostly in NJ, PA, and MD. It currently only offers auto insurance. It had revenues of $300M in 2013 and has seen a 5% slide in market share for each of the last 3 years. The US auto insurance industry had revenue of $3B in 2013. Major competitors are all currently exploring telematics options and operate in the same geographies.
prompt.question: The company has hired you to identify which telematics strategy — OBD or mobile app — is the right fit for them. They are also interested in understanding how to increase engagement with customers and provide additional services, specifically in states where AutoDrivers has low brand perception.

clarifying_info.a: Telematics is the convergence of informatics and telecommunications to transmit data, similar to how Fitbit or OnStar collect and use data to deliver services.

clarifying_info.q: What is the current market share of AutoDrivers?
clarifying_info.a: AutoDrivers had revenues of $300M in 2013; the US auto insurance industry had revenue of $3B in 2013, implying roughly 10% market share, though it has been declining 5% per year for 3 years.

clarifying_info.q: What products does AutoDrivers currently offer?
clarifying_info.a: AutoDrivers currently only offers auto insurance.

clarifying_info.q: What states does AutoDrivers operate in?
clarifying_info.a: AutoDrivers operates mostly in NJ, PA, and MD.

clarifying_info.q: What is AutoDrivers doing to increase customer engagement?
clarifying_info.a: Insurance is a commoditized business and companies are developing services such as competitions for safe drivers and teen-driving programs to differentiate themselves and increase customer engagement.
Yes, major competitors are all currently exploring telematics options and operate in the same geographies as AutoDrivers.

exhibits.title: OBD vs. Mobile Solution Comparison
exhibits.shows: A table comparing OBD and Mobile Solution across seven dimensions: potential customer size, potential market share, variable marketing cost per customer, variable equipment cost per customer, revenue per customer, customer adoption rate, technology development partner, and cost of technology development. All figures are expected over the next 3 years.

OBD.technology_development: Partner with a firm in NJ

Mobile_Solution.technology_development: Partner with a firm in China

exhibits.title: State-Level Telematics Opportunity
exhibits.shows: A bar chart showing the percentage of new customers interested in telematics by state (NJ, PA, MD), alongside a line chart showing the percentage increase in adoption rates over Year 1, Year 2, and Year 3 for each state. Brand perception data from a customer survey is also referenced.

framework: Market context: Understand AutoDrivers' competitive position — market share trend, revenue base, competitive dynamics with peers all exploring telematics
Technology fit: Evaluate OBD vs. mobile on implementation feasibility, build-vs-partner decision, development timeline, and technology trajectory
Financial analysis: Calculate addressable customers (market size × market share × adoption rate), variable margin per customer, and net profit after fixed technology development cost for each option
Customer engagement & differentiation: Assess which option better enables value-added services and improves brand perception in target geographies
Regulatory & adoption considerations: Assess regulatory risk (data privacy, state restrictions), customer adoption rates, and scalability
Pilot state selection: Use state-level data on telematics interest, brand perception, and adoption growth trajectory to identify optimal launch market

questions.prompt: Question 1: What are the first steps AutoDrivers should consider when deciding which telematics strategy to implement?
questions.guidance: A strong response covers: (1) margin comparison between OBD and mobile, (2) implementation timeline feasibility, (3) technology considerations — build internally vs. partner, (4) what competitors are doing. An advanced response also addresses: which option better enables customer engagement, regulatory considerations (data privacy, state government restrictions), and customer adoption rates.

questions.prompt: Question 2: Based on Exhibit 1, which strategy should AutoDrivers select? Calculate potential new customers and net profitability for each option.
questions.guidance: Candidate must calculate addressable new customers using market size × market share × adoption rate, then compute net profit as (margin per customer × new customers) − fixed cost. The mobile solution dominates on profitability.

math.setup: For each option: Addressable customers = Potential Customer Size × Potential Market Share × Adoption Rate. Variable cost per customer = marketing cost + equipment cost. Margin per customer = Revenue per customer − Variable cost per customer. Net Profit = Margin × Addressable customers − Fixed technology development cost.
math.answer: OBD net profit = −$750,000 (loss); Mobile Solution net profit = +$250,000. AutoDrivers should select the Mobile Solution.

questions.prompt: Question 3: What are the pros and cons of choosing the Mobile Solution? (Focus on non-financial factors.)
questions.guidance: A good candidate lists a few on each side; an excellent candidate shows understanding of mobile platforms and applications. Keep probing until the list is exhausted.

questions.prompt: Question 4: In which state should AutoDrivers pilot the Mobile Solution? Use Exhibit 2.
questions.guidance: NJ has the highest % of new customers interested in telematics (35%) and the highest brand perception, making it appear ideal. However, NJ's adoption rate increase over 3 years is lower than PA's. Since AutoDrivers wants to grow in states with low brand perception and increase customer engagement, PA is the best choice: it has the highest rate of increase in adoption (reaching ~20% by Year 3), giving AutoDrivers the best long-term market share reversal opportunity, and the Mobile Solution can help build brand perception through new features. The candidate should tie back to the original prompt's emphasis on growing in states with low brand perception.

brainstorming.prompt: What are the pros and cons of choosing the Mobile Solution over OBD?

categories.name: Pros of Mobile Solution
ideas: Ease of use — customers only need to download a mobile app, no hardware installation
High scalability for AutoDrivers across its geographies
Technology updates can be easily pushed to customers via app updates
Fits new customer demographics — mobile-first, flexible lifestyle
Mobile phone technology improves rapidly, enhancing data quality over time
High speed to market compared to hardware-dependent OBD

categories.name: Cons of Mobile Solution
ideas: Reliability of data capture — mobile technology for telematics is still under development
Partnering with a firm in China could increase development lead time and coordination complexity
Regulators could impose restrictions on collecting driving data via mobile phone
Higher capital expenditure ($2M vs. $0.9M for OBD)

recommendation: AutoDrivers should implement the Mobile Solution: it generates a net profit of $250,000 vs. a $750,000 loss for OBD, reaches more customers (500 vs. 250), and better fits the company's goals of increasing customer engagement through a scalable, easy-to-use platform.

AutoDrivers should pilot the Mobile Solution in Pennsylvania (PA): although NJ has higher current telematics interest and brand perception, PA has the highest projected increase in adoption rate over 3 years, aligns with the strategic goal of growing in states with low brand perception, and offers the greatest long-term opportunity to reverse the market share decline.
risks: How to address customer concerns over data privacy and surveillance
Potential barriers from state regulators and state governments restricting mobile-based driving data collection
Contingency plan if telematics adoption does not reach projected levels
Partner risk: relying on a Chinese firm may introduce development delays, IP concerns, or geopolitical risk
next_steps: Develop and negotiate a contract with the technology partner in China; validate their ability to deliver on time and at spec
Identify distribution channels for the Mobile Solution (insurance agents, third-party vendors, direct digital)
Select the right marketing strategy targeting PA customers, especially those with low brand awareness of AutoDrivers
Design and execute a testing program in PA to validate the mobile solution's data reliability and customer experience before broader rollout
Establish customer privacy and data governance policies to proactively address regulatory concerns
